name: ErrorSink
purpose: Capture uncaught exceptions with fingerprint grouping, attach current trace and correlation context, apply sampling, and forward to an error-tracking backend.
api_signature:
from typing import Protocol, Mapping, Callable

class ErrorSink(Protocol):
    def capture_exception(
        self,
        exc: BaseException,
        *,
        level: str = 'error',
        tags: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
        extras: Mapping[str, object] | None = None,
    ) -> str: ...
    def capture_message(self, message: str, *, level: str = 'error', tags: Mapping[str, str] | None = None) -> str: ...
    def register_fingerprinter(self, fn: Callable[[BaseException], list[str]]) -> None: ...
    def before_send(self, fn: Callable[[dict], dict | None]) -> None: ...
invariants: Every captured event MUST include the active trace_id, span_id, and request_id when any of those are set.
A fingerprint MUST be deterministic for the same exception type plus top-three stack frames; otherwise identical incidents SHALL NEVER split into separate issues.
capture_exception MUST redact registered PII field names (email, password, authorization) before transport.
The sink CANNOT block the caller; serialization and network transmission SHALL run on a background worker.
before_send hooks returning None MUST drop the event and NEVER partially transmit it.
Sampling SHALL apply AFTER fingerprinting so rare variants are not accidentally suppressed by head-of-queue drops.
extension_contract: Tools extend the sink by registering a fingerprinter callable that returns a list of grouping keys, by registering a before_send filter that redacts or drops events, and by implementing a TransportAdapter that speaks the target vendor's envelope while preserving the neutral event payload.

sources.locator: Chapter 5 'Structured Events Are the Building Blocks of Observability' pp. 57-62

sources.source: Google SRE Book — Monitoring Distributed Systems
sources.locator: Chapter 6 section 'Four Golden Signals' on error-rate grouping

why_essential: Per-tool error handling drops trace context and produces duplicate issues; one sink with fingerprinting and context-attachment is the only way to keep error groups stable and joinable to the originating trace.
alternatives_considered: Relying on log aggregation for errors — rejected because log pipelines lack fingerprint-based grouping and alert fatigue follows.
Per-framework exception middleware — rejected because background jobs, CLI, and consumers fall outside framework boundaries.
Raw stacktrace hashing as the only fingerprint — rejected because line-number drift from refactors splits stable issues.
